title: Cozmo stack source-fidelity manifest
about: One record per behaviour-affecting decision, or tightly bound group of decisions, in the hand-written
production code of cozmo-stack. Platform plumbing that cannot change what the robot does (logging,
collection choices, string formatting, file layout) is not recorded.
The manifest, not the prose documents, is the authoritative statement of what rests on primary source.
re-analysis/tools/fidelity.py validates it and regenerates FIDELITY_GAPS.md from it.
authority_order: the decompiled Unity C# (unity/scripts/csharp) and managed assemblies
the shipped Wwise banks, their .txt definition files, SoundbanksInfo.xml and PluginInfo.xml
the shipped OBB assets, configuration and animation data
CLAD / message schemas and the code generated from them
captures taken from the original app (re-analysis/captures)
existing reverse-engineering notes, only after checking them against the primary evidence above

statuses.EXACT_SOURCE: Read from primary source and reproduced. The record names the address, asset or schema it was read from.
statuses.EQUIVALENT_IMPLEMENTATION: The native behaviour is known from primary source and this stack reaches the same observable effect by a different mechanism. The record names the difference, and the difference has to be one a listener, a viewer or the robot cannot tell apart.
statuses.RECOVERABLE_GAP: A behaviour-affecting decision whose answer plausibly exists in primary source that has not been read, or has been read too shallowly to settle it. The work outstanding is reverse engineering.
statuses.IMPLEMENTATION_GAP: The native behaviour is established from primary evidence, and the production implementation knowingly does something else. The work outstanding is building it. This is unfinished fidelity work, not a policy.
statuses.COMPATIBILITY_POLICY: A deliberate product or platform decision this stack intends to keep: offline tools, the test harness, PC-side plumbing, or a stand-in the operator has to ask for. Not a place to put fidelity work that is hard.
statuses.HARDWARE_ONLY: No shipped artifact can settle it; only a robot, or a recording of the stock app, can.
statuses.BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: The answer lies in third-party code or data that is not in the package (Omron OKAO, the Wwise runtime DSP, the Acapela text-to-speech engine).

gate.rule: Two separate questions, and neither may be answered by the other. A subsystem's source investigation is exhausted only when it holds no RECOVERABLE_GAP on a live execution path; its implementation fidelity is complete only when it holds no IMPLEMENTATION_GAP there. A subsystem can have exhausted the source and still not reproduce what the source says, and neither state means the behaviour is faithfully reproduced: BLOCKED_EXTERNAL and HARDWARE_ONLY items can remain in both cases, and are counted separately so that they cannot be lost behind a single word.

field_notes.location: repository-relative path, optionally with :line, of the code the record is about
field_notes.effect: what a listener, viewer or the robot would observe if this decision were wrong
field_notes.provenance: what the current implementation actually rests on
field_notes.authority: the best available original evidence for this decision
field_notes.evidence: concrete references: native addresses, asset paths, bank object ids, capture files
field_notes.unresolved: for a RECOVERABLE_GAP, what has still to be read; for an IMPLEMENTATION_GAP, what has still to be built; empty string when nothing is
field_notes.hardware_required: whether a robot is genuinely needed to settle it
field_notes.live_path: whether the decision is reached on a normal run against a robot
field_notes.test: the regression that would fail if the recovered behaviour were undone

records.title: Only a ping marked as a reply measures the round trip
records.authority: ReliableConnection::ReceivePing 0x00835C70 branches on the byte at payload+0x10. Non-zero: the round trip is now - payload.timeSent, warned about if negative ("Ping has returned before it was sent!?") and added to a RecentStatsAccumulator sized by sMaxPingRoundTripsToTrack. Zero: the engine answers with SendPing(transport, payload.timeSent, true), but only when sSendSeparatePingMessages is set, and measures nothing. There is no third case
evidence: the payload is 17 bytes: f64 timeSent, u32 numPingsSent, u32 numPingsReceived, u8 isReply, and SendPing 0x00835BF2 writes exactly that, sending it as message type 0x0B
the counter bookkeeping matches too: numPingsReceived is incremented on receipt, and the pair is kept only when the incoming numPingsSent exceeds the last one seen

this stack also treated an echo of a timestamp it had sent as a reply, on the strength of a PyCozmo capture of the robot echoing with isReply clear. Against such a robot the app measures no round trip at all, so that clause is gone

records.title: Image chunk reassembly follows EncodedImage::AddChunk
records.provenance: EncodedImage::AddChunk 0x004F1CE0, read instruction by instruction
evidence: EncodedImage::AddChunk 0x004F1CE0 is the whole reassembly rule. A chunk whose payload is larger than 0x4B0 = 1200 bytes is refused before any bookkeeping (cmp.w r1, #0x4b0 at 0x004F1CF0, warning EncodedImage.AddChunk.ChunkTooBig).

One image is collected at a time: the chunk's image id is compared with the id held at +0x1C (0x004F1D38) and, when they differ, a new image starts there and then - buffer cleared, reserve(0x38400), chunk counter at +0x23 zeroed, expected chunk id at +0x21 zeroed. Whatever was being collected is simply gone; there is no queue of partial images.

The new image is valid (+0x22) only if its first chunk is chunk 0: cmp r0, #0 / moveq r0, #1 at 0x004F1D68. Its resolution must be 4, and the engine then writes 320 x 240 into the image (0x004F1D4E..0x004F1D58); any other resolution warns through EnumToString(ImageResolution) and the chunk goes no further.

The encoding at +0x20 is the chunk's own except that JPEGMinimizedGray (8) with a non-zero first payload byte becomes JPEGMinimizedColor (9): cmp r2, #0 / movne r2, #9 / cmp r1, #8 / movne r2, r1 at 0x004F1D8C.

Every chunk must carry the expected id or it warns ChunkOutOfOrder and clears the valid flag (0x004F1DB2..0x004F1DF4); the expected id becomes chunkId + 1 and the chunk counter rises. The last chunk is the one whose id is the announced count minus one (0x004F1E12), not simply one that carries a count - which is why a robot that sends the count only on the final chunk works.

On the last chunk the engine checks that it took exactly that many chunks (UnexpectedNumberOfChunks, 0x004F1E6A) and that the timestamp did not go backwards (TimestampNotIncreasing, 0x004F1E30), so the frame's timestamp is the one on its last chunk. Data is appended only while the image is valid (0x004F1EAE), and a last chunk on an invalidated image is the channel note "Received last chunk of invalidated image" rather than a frame.

The chunk field offsets the engine reads - +0 timestamp, +4 image id, +0xC encoding, +0xD resolution, +0xE chunk count, +0xF chunk id, +0x14 data - match this stack's ImageChunk layout field for field.

records.title: Trailing 0xFF strip, byte re-stuffing and EOI append
records.provenance: EncodedImage::MiniToJpegHelper 0x004F31C4
evidence: MiniGrayToJpeg 0x004F31A4 and MiniColorToJpeg 0x004F32D0 both call MiniToJpegHelper 0x004F31C4 with their header - 0x144 bytes at 0x00C48C40 and 0x14E bytes at 0x00C48D84 - which are the tables this stack already carries.

The helper reserves headerLen + 2 * size (0x004F31DE), inserts the header at the front, and patches the two 16-bit dimensions at output offsets 0x5E..0x61 (0x004F31F4..0x004F320C): its second argument first, which is the height, then the width. That is the 94 this stack uses.

It then walks back over the trailing 0xFF bytes (0x004F3214..0x004F321C), copies from index 1 rather than 0 - the loop counter starts at 2 and reads data[i - 1] at 0x004F3226, so the colour flag byte is dropped - appends a 0x00 after every 0xFF it copies (0x004F325A), and finishes with 0xFF 0xD9 at 0x004F3286 and 0x004F32AA. A payload of fewer than two bytes after the strip skips the copy (cmp r5, #2 at 0x004F321E).
Every step matches MiniJpeg.ToJpeg as it already stood; what was a PyCozmo transcription is now read from the engine.

records.title: Warm-up frames are flagged, and delivered like any other
records.effect: which frame a caller that asks for a picture gets first
records.provenance: a measurement of this hardware, kept as a flag on top of the engine's behaviour
evidence: The engine discards nothing at camera start-up. HandleImageChunk 0x00535A64 hands every image AddChunk completes to VisionComponent::SetNextImage (0x00535B94), and SetNextImage decodes it on the spot; the only drops on that path are invalid images and the per-tick cap recorded under M3-005. No symbol or string in libcozmoEngine.so speaks of skipping, warming up or settling frames.

So the fifteen-frame warm-up is this stack's own: the frames are flagged IsWarmUp and delivered like any other, the vision path sees all of them, and only CozmoRobot.CaptureFrameAsync waits past them, at its caller's option. The count comes from the firmware-2457 capture of 2026-09-18, where the picture is torn and rolls by one macroblock row per frame for about eleven frames.

records.title: One image is collected at a time, and three a tick reach vision
records.provenance: EncodedImage::AddChunk 0x004F1CE0 and HandleImageChunk 0x00535A64
evidence: There is no image queue to have a depth. AddChunk holds one image, keyed by the id at +0x1C, and a chunk with a different id starts a new one immediately (0x004F1D38), so a partial image is abandoned the moment the next one begins. This stack kept the newest two, which was a guess; it now keeps one.

The only other drop is per basestation tick. HandleImageChunk 0x00535A64 compares the event's time with the last tick it saw (the double at +0x130): a new tick zeroes the counter at +0x128 and the image goes to VisionComponent::SetNextImage; within one tick the counter rises and an image whose count reaches 3 is dropped with "Ignoring %dth image (with t=%u) received during basestation tick at %fsec" (0x00535B46..0x00535B6C). The same counter gates forwarding chunks to the game at 0x00535AAC.
At the 15 frames a second this camera produces against a 30 Hz tick a second complete image inside one tick cannot arise, so the cap is recorded as CozmoCamera.MaxImagesPerTick and not counted.

records.title: The face encoder is the engine's: skip, repeat, runs and the raw fallback
evidence: FaceAnimationManager::CompressRLE 0x00581904 builds one 64-bit mask per column, bit r for canvas row r: the ^ 0x3F at 0x005819A0 is part of computing the two shift amounts, not a flip - row 0 lands on bit 0 (lsr of 0x80000000 by 31) and row 63 on bit 63
an empty column (0x00581B0A) counts the consecutive empty columns that follow under r5 + r3 <= 0x7E and r3 <= 0x3E and emits the count alone, command 00, advancing by count + 1
a column equal to the one before (0x00581A0A) counts the same way and emits 0x40 | (count - 1) at 0x00581B54, where the adds r0, #0xff is the minus one

otherwise it walks the mask two bits at a time and emits 0x7C + 4 * length or'd with the pair and with 0x80 (0x00581A6C), which is exactly 0x80 | (length-1) << 2 for 1..16 and 0xC0 | (length-17) << 2 for 17..32
a trailing blank run is dropped unless the next column is both non-empty and different (0x00581ABC..0x00581AE2), which is what lets the following skip or repeat do the column advance
above 1024 bytes the RLE is thrown away and the raw 1024-byte mask buffer is sent instead (size >> 10 non-zero at 0x00581B7E, then a resize to 0x400 and a byte copy)

the decoder here had two flags where one will do, and had the skip command consult the wrong one; the 28 sequences Cozmo itself produced decode identically either way, and a column ending on a drawn run followed by an empty column is the case that tells them apart
records.prior: runs only, every column padded to 32 rows, no skip, no repeat, and an image whose RLE was too big refused instead of sent raw

records.title: Audio frames are sent reliably
records.provenance: AnimationStreamer::SendBufferedMessages 0x0057BF60 and UpdateAmountToSend 0x0057C6F0
evidence: SendBufferedMessages 0x0057BF60 walks the streamer's buffered EngineToRobot messages and for each one reads the tag and masks it: and r0, r0, #0xfe; cmp r0, #0x8e (0x0057BF8C) sets r5 = 1 for an audio frame, which is animAudioSample 0x8E or animAudioSilence 0x8F.

It then calls Robot::SendMessage(EngineToRobot const&, bool reliable, bool hot) with movs r2, #1 and movs r3, #0 at 0x0057BFA6, for the audio frames and for everything else alike - so audio is reliable and not hot, and nothing in the streamer sends anything unreliably.

What varies is the amount, not the reliability: the streamer holds a byte budget at +0x98 and an audio-frame budget at +0x9C, stops when the next message is over the byte budget (cmp r4, r1; bhi) or the audio budget has no room (cmp r0, r5; blt), and decrements both by what it sent (0x0057BFB0..0x0057BFB8).

UpdateAmountToSend 0x0057C6F0 refills them from four counters the robot reports at Robot+0x238: bytes played, bytes streamed, audio frames played, audio frames streamed. The byte budget is min(8192 - (streamed - played), 30000) - add.w r5, r0, #0x2000 then movw r0, #0x7530 and the lt select at 0x0057C79C - and the audio budget is 14 - (streamed - played), add.w r1, r1, #0xe, each clamped at zero; a negative byte budget logs the warning AnimationStreamer.UpdateAmountToSend.NegativeMinBytesFreeInRobot with "minBytesFree:%d numBytesStreamed:%d numBytesPlayed:%d".
CozmoRobot.AudioReliable therefore defaults to true because that is what the engine does. The switch itself is this stack's own addition for a lossy link, documented as such.

records.title: Motion is gated on calibration here; the engine reacts to it instead
records.effect: whether a direct motor command during calibration is sent or refused
records.provenance: a default of this stack over the engine's behaviour-layer response, which is implemented
records.authority: HandleMotorCalibration 0x00536A68, BehaviorReactToMotorCalibration 0x006065F0, and the callers of IsHeadCalibrated / IsLiftCalibrated, all read
evidence: The engine does not gate motion on calibration. Robot::IsHeadCalibrated 0x00512378 and Robot::IsLiftCalibrated 0x005151A6 are called only by RobotGyroDriftDetector::DetectGyroDrift, CalibrateMotorAction::CheckIfDone, BehaviorReactToImpact::AlwaysHandle and BehaviorReactToMotorCalibration::HandleWhileRunning; MovementComponent::MoveHeadToAngle 0x006407CC and MoveLiftToHeight 0x00640700 send what they are given.

RobotToEngineImplMessaging::HandleMotorCalibration 0x00536A68 reads the message's three bytes - motorID, calibStarted, autoStarted - sets the calibrated flag to !calibStarted for MOTOR_HEAD (3) at 0x00536BCE and MOTOR_LIFT (2) at 0x00536BE4, calls CarryingComponent::SetCarriedObjectAsUnattached when the lift starts calibrating while carrying something (0x00536BB8), and broadcasts the message to the game.

BehaviorReactToMotorCalibration::InitInternal 0x006065F0 is the engine's actual response: SmartDisableReactionsWithLock, then a WaitAction of 5 seconds (0x40A00000 at 0x00606650), with HandleWhileRunning ending it early once both motors report calibrated. This stack implements that as ReactToMotorCalibrationBehavior, with the same 5 seconds and the same reaction lock.

The message-layer refusal in CozmoMotion.NotReady is therefore this stack's own default, kept because a caller here can command a motor directly where the engine's callers are behaviours the reaction has already displaced. Every caller can pass requireCalibration: false.

records.title: Cliff sensors named from the engine's enum; IMU and cube battery in the engine's units
records.provenance: EnumToString(CliffSensor), DetectGyroDrift, the off-treads classifier and HandleObjectPowerLevel, all read
evidence: The cliff order is the engine's CliffSensor enum: EnumToString(CliffSensor) 0x007D292C bounds the value at 4 and indexes the pointer table at 0x01034C50, which holds "CLIFF_FL", "CLIFF_FR", "CLIFF_BL", "CLIFF_BR", "CLIFF_COUNT" in that order. The same index space reaches the readings: CliffSensorComponent::UpdateRobotData 0x00634016 copies the four 16-bit values out of RobotState at +0x50 and +0x54 as two words, in order, and GetCliffDataRaw(i) reads them back. So bit 0 is front-left and bit 3 back-right, which is what CliffSensors now says.

The gyro is in radians per second. DetectGyroDrift 0x0052C568 reads the z rate at RobotState +0x44 and calls the robot still only while its magnitude is at or under 0.174533 - 10 degrees a second - at 0x0052C580, then compares successive samples against 0.0174533 (one degree) and a pose delta against 0.00872665 (half a degree). The accelerometer is in millimetres per second squared: the engine's own off-treads classifier takes gravity to be 9800 in these units (OffTreadsClassifier.GravityAccel, already recorded under M10), and Robot::UpdateFullRobotState 0x0051291C reads the three axes at RobotState +0x30, +0x34 and +0x38 and filters them unscaled (0x00512A36..0x00512A6E).

The offsets line up with this stack's RobotState layout exactly - status at +0x4C, cliff data at +0x50, accel at +0x30 and gyro at +0x3C - which is a second confirmation of that layout.

evidence: HandleActiveObjectAvailable 0x0053391C reads the factory id at +0, the object type at +4 and the RSSI at +8, and records the advertisement only when IsValidLightCube 0x007D1D08 or IsCharger 0x007D1D50 says yes (0x00533944 and 0x00533954). records.title: An audio keyframe's volume is the Event_Volume trim, not a gain
records.provenance: RobotAudioAnimationOnRobot::BeginBufferingAudioOnRobotMode and the shipped banks, read
records.authority: RobotAudioAnimationOnRobot::BeginBufferingAudioOnRobotMode 0x00598298 and the Event_Volume bindings in the shipped banks, read
evidence: The keyframe volume goes to Wwise as a game parameter, not to the samples. RobotAudioAnimationOnRobot::BeginBufferingAudioOnRobotMode posts the event with RobotAudioClient::PostCozmoEvent (0x0059826C), keeps the playing id it returns, and calls RobotAudioClient::SetCozmoEventParameter(playingId, parameter, value) at 0x00598298 with r2 = 0xD2687048 and the volume from the audio ref at +0xC, then ProcessEvents.
0xD2687048 is the FNV-1 hash of "Event_Volume", which is one of the parameter names in the bank definition text.

In the shipped banks that parameter is bound to the Volume property of three actor mixers - 62050212 and 682998829 in Cozmo.bnk, 121198006 in Dev_Debug.bnk - with accumulate 1 (additive) and a curve from (0, -1) to (1, 0). Volume is in decibels, so the whole range of the keyframe volume is one decibel of trim: 1.0 leaves the event alone, 0.0 takes one decibel off it, and nothing about it is silence.

This stack multiplied the PCM by the volume, so a keyframe volume of 0 was silence and 0.5 was half amplitude - about six decibels down where the engine is half of one. WwiseAudioSource now reads the binding out of the loaded banks and converts the volume through its curve, so the gain is 10^(dB/20) and a bank set that binds the parameter differently is followed.

records.title: The last face is held after the last face keyframe, and no face the engine sends is oversize
records.provenance: SendEndOfAnimation and BufferFaceToSend, read

records.title: Stereo IMA ADPCM: the block is two mono blocks side by side
records.provenance: the seven shipped stereo files, decoded; the layout is arithmetic the files either fit or do not
records.authority: the shipped stereo ADPCM media in Cozmo.bnk - their fmt headers and their data
evidence: The header settles the block. All seven stereo files are 48000 Hz with nAvgBytesPerSec 54000 and nBlockAlign 72, so 750 blocks a second and 64 samples per channel in each. A 36-byte mono block holds exactly 64 samples ((36 - 4) * 2), so a 72-byte stereo block is two of them: the left channel's four-byte header and thirty-two bytes of nibbles, then the right channel's.

The bytes agree. Read that way, all 226 per-channel headers across the seven files (113 blocks each) carry a step index inside the table's 0..88; read as two four-byte headers followed by one run of nibbles, between 50 and 67 of every 226 are out of range. Decoding the seven gives 7232 samples per channel each, peaks of 4430, 18259, 18916, 23387, 25453 and twice full scale, and the two that touch the rails do so 2 and 14 times in 14464 samples - ordinary near-full-scale content, not a decoder running away.

The eight events that reach those files - Play__Robot_SFX__Effort_Long, Effort_Medium, Effort_Fail, Spark_Launch, Scan_Loop_Play, Scan_Start, Scan_Stop and Scan_Single - now render audio instead of nothing.

Which half is the left channel is the one thing the bytes cannot say; the natural order is taken (channel 0 first), and swapping it would swap the stereo image of eight sound effects played through a mono speaker.

records.title: Scored selection: emotion scorers or the flat score, times the penalties
records.provenance: ReadFromScoredJson, EvaluateScore, EvaluateScoreInternal and MoodScorer, read
records.authority: IBehavior::ReadFromScoredJson 0x005BC488, IBehavior::EvaluateScore 0x005BEF60, IBehavior::EvaluateScoreInternal 0x005BEEC2 and MoodScorer::EvaluateEmotionScore 0x0067C9B8, read
evidence: ReadFromScoredJson 0x005BC488 reads four things: "emotionScorers" into a MoodScorer at +0xDC, "flatScore" into the float at +0x100, "repetitionPenalty" into the GraphEvaluator2d at +0xE8, and "considerThisHasRunForBehaviorObjective" into a behaviour objective. A repetitionPenalty that is missing or unreadable warns (IScoredBehavior.BadRepetitionPenalty) and leaves the graph empty, and an empty graph gets the single node AddNode(0, 1, true) at 0x005BC55E - a flat penalty of one.

EvaluateScoreInternal 0x005BEEC2 is the rule this stack had wrong: if the MoodScorer's list is not empty it tail-calls MoodScorer::EvaluateEmotionScore and that is the score; only an empty list falls through to the flat score at +0x100. The two are alternatives, not addends.

MoodScorer::EvaluateEmotionScore 0x0067C9B8 walks the scorers, evaluates each one's graph at its emotion's value - or at the value minus the value sixty ticks ago when trackDelta is set (Emotion::GetHistoryValueTicksAgo(60) at 0x0067C9F4) - and returns the mean of the results (0x0067CA6E..0x0067CA72). A scorer whose graph comes out within 1e-05 of zero (0x0067CA50) ends the walk and the whole score is zero.

EvaluateScore 0x005BEF60 wraps it: while the behaviour runs it uses the running score plus the float at +0x104 and multiplies by EvaluateRunningPenalty when +0x111 is set; otherwise it scores only a behaviour that IsRunnableBase and wants to run.

EmotionScorer::ReadFromJson 0x0067AABC names the three keys: emotionType, scoreGraph, trackDelta. Not one shipped behaviour or activity config carries an emotionScorers block, so every scored behaviour in the app is scored by its flatScore alone; the sixty-tick history this stack does not keep is therefore never reached, and is marked LOCAL_POLICY where it would be.

records.title: PlayAnim plays every trigger it lists, in order, num_loops times
records.provenance: BehaviorPlayAnimSequence, read
evidence: StartPlayingAnimations 0x005C0158 measures the trigger vector at +0x11C: a byte length of exactly 4 - one trigger - is special-cased and played as a single TriggerLiftSafeAnimationAction with the loop count from +0x128 (0x005C0190). Anything else falls through to StartSequenceLoop.

StartSequenceLoop 0x005C0294 runs while the counter at +0x12C is below the loop count at +0x128: it makes a CompoundActionSequential and walks the whole trigger vector, adding one TriggerLiftSafeAnimationAction per trigger (0x005C02CA..0x005C030E), then runs the compound and increments the counter. So every trigger plays, in the config's order, and the list repeats.
The loop count is the config's num_loops, read with a default of 1: Json::Value::Value(1) then Json::Value::get("num_loops", default) at 0x005C001C..0x005C0036.

Of the fifteen shipped PlayAnim configs, one lists more than one trigger - NothingToDo_BoredAnim, whose own comment calls its intro, event and outro a "sequence of anims" - and none sets num_loops. This stack played the first trigger that resolved and stopped; it now plays the list.

records.title: An action's track mask is a lock, taken while it runs
records.provenance: IActionRunner::Update and MovementComponent::LockTracks, read
evidence: Every action carries a track mask at +0x54. IActionRunner::Update 0x00540370 reads it and asks MovementComponent::AreAnyTracksLocked(mask) at 0x00540440: while any of those tracks is held it warns "Action %s [%d] not running because required tracks are locked" (0x005404A8) and does not run the action - it stays queued and is tried again on the next tick. Otherwise it locks them through the helper at 0x004F0F4C, which calls MovementComponent::LockTracks(mask, tag, name), and then runs the action.

LockTracks 0x00640098 walks the bits of the mask and inserts one LockInfo - the owner's name and reason - per track into a multiset at component+0x30; UnlockTracks 0x0063FE5C removes them. So a track is held by a set of owners and is free when the last one lets go.

The mask is therefore mutual exclusion, not muting: the animation plays its tracks and nothing else may drive them while it does. This stack claims the clip's tracks on the behaviour's scope and the scheduler refuses a play whose tracks are owned, which is the same arrangement; the refusal now waits and retries, as IActionRunner does, instead of treating the play as done.

The third argument of PlayTrigger was a suppressTracks mask whose note claimed the engine mutes a track for one play. It is now alsoLock, and it is added to the scope's claim: BehaviorReactToUnexpectedMovement's tracksToLock of 4 means the reaction holds the body track while it plays, which keeps the keep-alive and anything else off the wheels - not that the animation's own body track is silenced.

records.title: The head recalibration wait: the engine has no timeout, this stack keeps a backstop
records.effect: how long a behaviour sits out a recalibration that never finishes
records.provenance: CalibrateMotorAction and IAction's default timeout, read; the five seconds is this stack's
evidence: CalibrateMotorAction::CheckIfDone 0x00547D38 is the whole completion rule: it stays running until the motors it was asked for report calibrated, testing Robot::IsHeadCalibrated and IsLiftCalibrated against the request flags at +0x78 and +0x79 and the already-started flags at +0x7A and +0x7B, and returns the running marker 0x01000000 until then.

There is no timeout behind it. IAction's constructor writes -1 to the action's timeout at +0x74 (movs r1, #0 / movt r1, #0xbf80 at 0x00540CA2), which is the engine's "no timeout", and CalibrateMotorAction does not override it. So the engine waits as long as it takes.

This stack waits five seconds and carries on. That is a backstop, not a reading: a wait that never ends is not worth reproducing, and five seconds is what the engine's own behaviours give a recalibration when they sit one out - BehaviorReactToImpact's WaitAction and BehaviorReactToMotorCalibration's, both 0x40A00000. The robot reports in about two.

records.title: The sub-pixel corner refinement
records.effect: a refined corner lands in a slightly different place than the engine would put it, so the marker pose does too
records.provenance: the corner extraction is now the engine's (QuadCorners); what is still local is the refinement this stack applies afterwards
records.authority: ComputeQuadrilateralsFromConnectedComponents 0x00892D70, TraceNextExteriorBoundary 0x008C6B18, ExtractLineFitsPeaks 0x008A5DB8, Quadrilateral<float>::ComputeClockwiseCorners 0x008A1324 and IsQuadrilateralReasonable 0x00892B18, all read and implemented; VisionMarker::RefineCorners 0x0089FD98 and RefineQuadrilateral 0x008C55E0 (3980 bytes), not read
evidence: The corner extraction is transcribed. TraceNextExteriorBoundary 0x008C6B18 builds its staircase contour from four extent arrays over the component's bounding box in four passes, dropping points past the 10000 the caller allocates (0x00892DA8) and failing on an empty row or column; ExtractLineFitsPeaks 0x008A5DB8 differentiates a Gaussian of sigma = length / 64 (0x3C800000, with OpenCV's size relation solved backwards at 0x008A5ED6), convolves it circularly with the boundary in double and normalises, seeds four equal arcs and runs cv::kmeans with KMEANS_USE_INITIAL_LABELS, one attempt, 15 iterations and epsilon 0.1 (0x008A6490) - so nothing is random - fits each cluster across its wider extent (the swapped flag at 0x008A6714), intersects all six pairs keeping only the four inside the image (0x008A6BE2), orders them by atan2 about their centroid ascending (0x008A1324) and rounds half away from zero into an s16 quad.

So is the acceptance test and the order the quad is kept in: the clockwise corners permuted 0, 3, 1, 2 (0x00892E88), IsQuadrilateralReasonable's four rules on that order, and the middle pair exchanged when it reports the other winding (0x00892B7E and 0x00892F04).

What is left is the refinement. DetectFiducialMarkers calls VisionMarker::RefineCorners 0x0089FD98, which calls RefineQuadrilateral 0x008C55E0 - 3980 bytes, not read - and this stack instead walks each side of the quad looking for the strongest dark-to-light step along its normal and re-fits the four lines, up to 25 times. On rendered markers the corners land within 1 px of truth and PnP reprojection is 0.1 to 0.4 px, so the difference is small, but it is a difference and the source for it exists.

What it is, is read even though it is not transcribed: VisionMarker::RefineCorners 0x0089FD98 takes the marker's own bright and dark values (ComputeBrightDarkValues) and its homography, and RefineQuadrilateral 0x008C55E0 runs a Gauss-Newton refinement of that homography - samples laid along the four edges of the canonical square either side of each one, an offset scaled by (bright - dark) and the longer diagonal, Matrix::Multiply and MakeSymmetric into a normal-equation system, SolveLeastSquaresWithCholesky, and Invert3x3 to apply the update - under the parameters this stack already reads off Parameters::Initialize: 25 iterations, a 0.005 minimum change, a 5.0 maximum, and the 1.01 step growth.

The pose the refined corners feed is a separate matter and not a gap: the engine hands cv::solvePnP four corners inside Camera::ComputeObjectPoseHelper, and PoseEstimation.cs solves the same problem with its own numerics - a different mechanism for the same answer, and it recovers a cube pose to under a millimetre and half a degree in test.

How far it was traced, so the next pass does not start over: RefineQuadrilateral's arguments land at [sp+0x380] onwards - the second scale point, an int, bright, dark, the sample count, two more floats, the out quad, the out homography and the memory stack. It takes the longer of the two diagonals (0x008C5620), allocates five 1-by-N float arrays with N = 8 * ceil(count / 8), and fills them in four near-identical blocks, one per edge of the canonical square, with an offset of (dark - bright) / 255 * 0.5 * (diagonal / sqrt(2)) either side of the edge (0x008C583C..0x008C585E). Then the iteration: Matrix::Multiply and MakeSymmetric into a normal-equation system, SolveLeastSquaresWithCholesky, Invert3x3 and the homography update. What is not settled is the sampling and the Jacobian in detail, and transcribing those from the register plumbing alone would be guesswork rather than recovery.
records.unresolved: RefineQuadrilateral 0x008C55E0: the sampling pattern along each edge and the Jacobian of the homography update. Its arguments, its offset formula and its solver are read

Detect projects it, filters the bounding rectangle with the seven-by-five kernel at 0x00C8E020 (identical for the colour and grey paths), masks everything outside the quad away (fillConvexPoly of the quad's corners 0, 2, 3, 1 then SetMaskTo), transposes and walks each column from the bottom up for the first response past the threshold of 50 that VisionSystem constructs it with (0x006B0120). Image points become ground points through the homography, refused when its third component is not positive (0x006AE0A8). The lift is a gate rather than a mask: unless the first of two points on it projects below the ROI rectangle, or the second above it, the frame is abandoned (0x006AC4A2..0x006ACDC8). Points join a chain while they are of the same kind and within 5 mm (0x006AE1B0).

The map side. AddVisionOverheadEdges puts each point in world coordinates through the robot's pose at the frame's timestamp, splits the ray at the ROI's near edge and asks HasCollisionRayWithTypes about each half with the two masks at 0x00C8768B and 0x00C876A1, and accumulates runs that hold their direction to within forty degrees (0.766 at 0x0067F980). A run longer than the noise length (the literal 6.00001 at 0x0067FA14) becomes the triangle between the robot and its ends as ClearOfObstacle, or a line to its midpoint when the run is under fifteen millimetres (225 as a squared length at 0x0067FF5C); a run from a border chain also goes in as a two-point InterestingEdge (the type byte 9 at 0x006802AC). records.title: The dark mask and the quad acceptance test are the engine's
records.provenance: ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial, BinomialFilter, IsQuadrilateralReasonable and the parameters they are given, read
records.authority: ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial 0x00890448, ImageProcessing::BinomialFilter 0x008A2344, IsQuadrilateralReasonable 0x00892B18, ComputeQuadrilateralsFromConnectedComponents 0x00892D70, MarkerDetector::Parameters::Initialize 0x008752F8 and the call in DetectFiducialMarkers at 0x00898C18, read
evidence: The dark test is a filtered value and a Q16 multiplier, not a fraction of a box mean. ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial 0x00890448 runs one pass per pyramid level - DownsampleByTwo, BinomialFilter, |filtered - image| as the response (Matrix::Elementwise::ApplyOperation<SumOfAbsDiff> at 0x008907F4), UpsampleByPowerOfTwoBilinear back to full size - and its "ecvcsB_scale_select" loop at 0x00890B14 keeps the filtered value wherever the response beats the best so far. Its "ecvcsB_binarize" loop at 0x00890BB6 then marks a pixel dark when (scale * multiplier) >> 16 > pixel.

The two numbers come from the parameters DetectFiducialMarkers hands it at 0x00898C18: the word at +4 is the number of pyramid levels and Initialize sets it to 1 (0x0087530E), and the word at +0xC is the threshold multiplier, 0xCCCC (0x00875314), which is 0.79998779 in Q16. This stack had a three-level box pyramid and a local guess of 0.75.

BinomialFilter 0x008A2344 (coretech vision/robot/src/filtering.cpp) is the separable five-tap [1 4 6 4 1] with a >> 4 after each pass (the interior at 0x008A2490..0x008A24A6), and at the borders the off-image taps take the edge pixel: the first column's weights fold into 11, 4, 1 (0x008A243C) and the second's into 5, 6, 4, 1 (0x008A2458).

IsQuadrilateralReasonable 0x00892B18 is four tests in order: the cross product of the first three corners must reach quads_minQuadArea in absolute value (0x00892B5C), the cross products the diagonals make must agree in sign (0x00892C68, 0x00892CCA), one diagonal's two triangles must satisfy max << 8 < threshold * min (0x00892CFC..0x00892D22), and every corner must be at least the margin from each edge (0x00892D3A). ComputeQuadrilateralsFromConnectedComponents passes them from the parameters' +0x30, +0x34 and +0x38: 25, 512 - which is 2.0 in 8.8, not the maximum number of quads this stack had recorded - and 2.

ComputeTurnTowardsImagePointAngles 0x0051879C subtracts the calibration's centre from the point (the two-float loop at 0x005187CC), takes the historical state at the image's timestamp through RobotStateHistory::ComputeStateAt, and computes atan2(-(v - cy), fy) for the head (0x0054886C with the focal length at calibration+8) and atan2(-(u - cx), fx) for the body (0x0051888E, focal length at +4). The head angle is added to the head angle in that state and the body angle to its heading, so both come out absolute.

TurnTowardsImagePointAction 0x0054B59C is a PanAndTiltAction: Init 0x0054B664 asks for those two angles, writes them into the pan and tilt fields at +0x114 and +0x11C, and runs PanAndTiltAction::Init. When the history cannot answer it warns "TurnTowardsImagePointAction.Init.ComputeTurnTowardsImagePointAnglesFailed" and turns nowhere.
This stack aimed at a point 200 mm along the ray through the pixel, a range it invented, and then turned towards that pose. It now computes the same two angles and pans and tilts to them.

records.title: The memory map, and the question the face behaviour asks it before driving in
records.provenance: CanDriveIdealDistanceForward, TransitionToDrivingForward, the content-type table, the family mapping and the two insertion paths, read
records.authority: BehaviorInteractWithFaces::CanDriveIdealDistanceForward 0x005C2420, BehaviorInteractWithFaces::TransitionToDrivingForward 0x005C254E, MemoryMap::HasCollisionRayWithTypes 0x0068176E, ObjectFamilyToMemoryMapContentType 0x0067F4C0, MapComponent::AddObservableObject 0x0067ECFC, BlockWorld::AddMarkerlessObject 0x00622380, the EContentType names at 0x00BFFAC8 and the mask at 0x00C67962, read
evidence: The question is a ray. CanDriveIdealDistanceForward 0x005C2420 takes the local point (40, 0, 0) (0x42200000 at 0x005C2442), turns it by the robot's rotation, adds the robot's translation, and calls the memory map's virtual at +0x30 with the two x,y pairs and the type array at 0x00C67962, returning the negation (0x005C24A4). HasCollisionRayWithTypes 0x0068176E folds the array into a flag mask - EContentTypeToFlag for every entry whose bool is set - and hands it to the quad tree's ray walk.

The mask is eleven (type, bool) pairs: 00 00, 01 00, 02 00, 03 01, 04 01, 05 00, 06 01, 07 01, 08 01, 09 01, 0a 01. With the names from the table at 0x00BFFAC8 - Unknown, ClearOfObstacle, ClearOfCliff, ObstacleObservable, ObstacleCharger, ObstacleChargerRemoved, ObstacleProx, ObstacleUnrecognized, Cliff, InterestingEdge, NotInterestingEdge - everything blocks the drive except the first three and ObstacleChargerRemoved.

The answer changes the distance, not whether it drives. TransitionToDrivingForward loads -15.0 (vmov.f32 s0, #-15.0 at 0x005C2566) and replaces it with 40.0 only when the call returned true (0x005C2572), then builds DriveStraightAction(robot, distance, 40.0) - so a blocked robot backs off 15 mm. This stack drove 40 mm at 50 mm/s either way.

What goes in the map: MapComponent::AddObservableObject 0x0067ECFC inserts the object's bounding quad (its virtual GetBoundingQuadXY(pose, 0), vtable +0x50) with a MemoryMapData_ObservableObject, whose constructor 0x00684A38 stamps content type 3; ObjectFamilyToMemoryMapContentType 0x0067F4C0 is the tbb that decides it - Block, LightCube and CustomObject give ObstacleObservable on add and ClearOfObstacle on remove, the charger gives ObstacleCharger and ObstacleChargerRemoved, Ramp and Mat give Unknown, and a markerless object is refused with "ContentType MarkerlessObject addition is not supported". BlockWorld::AddMarkerlessObject 0x00622380 inserts a Cliff (type 8) for a CliffDetection object and a ProxObstacle (type 6) for a ProxObstacle one, and nothing for a CollisionObstacle (the type test at 0x0062259A falls through) - so the obstacle an unexpected movement leaves behind is in the world model and never in the map.

Implemented as Vision/MemoryMap.cs: the eleven content types, the family mapping, the mask, Insert, HasCollisionRayWithTypes and a sync that follows the world model's located objects, with the behaviour asking it before it drives. The engine keeps its regions in a quad tree (QuadTree 0x00684C08) subdivided to GetContentPrecisionMM; this keeps the polygons, which answers the same ray exactly rather than to the tree's precision. The map's vision-derived content - the overhead edges that become InterestingEdge and NotInterestingEdge, and the explored region the robot's own passage leaves - is M11-017.

records.title: Needs decay modifiers, damaged parts and persistence
records.provenance: NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers, NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel and the NeedsManager's device write, read, with the shipped configs
records.authority: NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers 0x0069C214, NeedsState::NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel 0x0069CCAC, NeedsManager::WriteToDevice 0x00693BB0 and NeedsFilenameFromSerialNumber 0x00695224, read
evidence: One need scales another's decay through an array of three multipliers. NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers 0x0069C214 starts them at one and, for each need, takes its level and walks that need's modifier list: every entry whose threshold the level is at or under multiplies the listed other need's entry (the compare at 0x0069C270, the multiply and store at 0x0069C2A4). ApplyDecayAllNeeds 0x00695CFE asks for them once and passes the array to NeedsState::ApplyDecay, so the whole pass uses one set.

The shipped needs_decay_config.json carries ConnectedDecayModifiersEnergy and ConnectedDecayModifiersRepair. Every entry multiplies by one except Repair's at 0.03, which doubles Play: while Repair is at or below 0.03, Play decays twice as fast. That is the only modifier in the shipped data that changes anything.

Damaged parts follow the Repair level. NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel 0x0069CCAC walks the broken-part thresholds in order and counts the leading run that is at or above the level, stopping at the first below it (0x0069CCC8). The thresholds are needs_config.json's BrokenPartThreshold0..2 - 0.98, 0.6 and 0.3 - so a full robot has none damaged, below 0.98 one, below 0.6 two and below 0.3 three. RepairRounds is 1. Which part is picked (PickPartToDamage 0x0069CCDE, PickPartToRepair 0x0069CD30) is cosmetic and is not modelled.

Persistence is per robot and carries a timestamp. NeedsFilenameFromSerialNumber 0x00695224 builds a prefix, an underscore (0x006952FC) and the serial with ".json" on the end; WriteToDevice 0x00693BB0 writes the levels with system_clock::now() divided by a million, that is whole seconds; and ApplyDecayForTimeSinceLastDeviceWrite 0x00695304 decays for the elapsed time when the file is read back, with InitAfterSerialNumberAcquired, StartReadFromRobot and InitAfterReadFromRobotAttempt ordering the startup. NeedsManager.Save and Load are that, with the path left to the host as the engine leaves it to the app.

records.title: The flat 3 s cooldown for an activity that ended as soon as it started
records.provenance: IActivityStrategy::WantsToStart and its call site, read
evidence: The two float arguments are the activity's own times, read together at the call site: ldrd r3, r2, [r1, #0x54] at 0x005B26FE gives r3 = +0x54 and r2 = +0x58, and WantsToStart measures the cooldown from the second (0x005B531C adds the cooldown to it) - so +0x58 is the last end time and +0x54 the last start.

Their difference is the length of the last run: s22 = arg2 - arg3 at 0x005B52EA. The engine asks BaseStationTimer::GetTimeSinceLastTickInSeconds (0x005B52F2), doubles it (0x005B5304), and when the run was positive but no longer than that - two ticks - it uses a flat 3 seconds (vmov.f32 s0, #3.0 at 0x005B5312) in place of the configured cooldown at +0x20.

The rest of the test is as recorded: no cooldown at all below the 1e-05 epsilon, no wait for an activity that has never ended unless startInCooldown is set (+0x28), and on passing, the cooldown is re-randomised as base (+0x1C) plus RandDbl(randomness at +0x24).
This stack now records the start time alongside the end time and applies the three seconds.

records.title: Activity deselection hook and the null-pick path
records.provenance: IActivity::OnDeselected, IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior and ActivityFreeplay::GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal, read end to end
records.authority: IActivity::OnDeselected 0x005B33B8, IActivity::OnSelected 0x005B312C, IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior 0x005B387C, ActivityFreeplay::GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal 0x005AE29C, ActivityFreeplay::PickNewActivityForSpark 0x005ADC44, SelectionBSRunnableChooser::OnDeselected 0x0060AF64, NeedsManager::SparksRewardCommunicatedToUser 0x00696E64, BehaviorEarnedSparks::StopInternal 0x005DAF70, read
evidence: The deselection hook is IActivity::OnDeselected 0x005B33B8, and it runs in this order: stamp the end time at +0x58 (OnSelected stamps the start at +0x54, 0x005B3142); call the chooser's hook, its vtable +0x24, of which only SelectionBSRunnableChooser::OnDeselected 0x0060AF64 does anything - it disables its selected behaviour's info-analyzer process, the mirror of OnSelected 0x0060AF20; remove the idle animation from the AnimationStreamer (robot+0x60) and the driving animations from the handler (robot+0x24c), each keyed by the activity's debug name and each only if the config named one (+0x44, +0x38 against 0x23f); drop the AIInformationAnalyzer enable request (+0x48); release every SmartDisableReactions lock in the set at +0x5c and destroy the set; SmartRemoveIdleAnimation if the pushed flag at +0x50 is set; clear the current-behaviour shared_ptr at +0x2c; and log robot.freeplay_goal_ended with the duration in whole seconds, a negative one raising "IActivity.Exit.NegativeDuration".

One thing in that list was missing here: if the needs manager still has a freeplay sparks reward pending (+0x3d8), OnDeselected calls NeedsManager::SparksRewardCommunicatedToUser (0x005B3548). That routine 0x00696E64 clears the flag and sends FreeplaySparksAwarded with the amount at +0x3dc. Its other two callers are BehaviorEarnedSparks::StopInternal 0x005DAF70 - which tests the byte and tail-calls it, so the reward is communicated when that behaviour *stops*, not when it starts, as this stack had it - and RegisterNeedsActionCompleted 0x006963C0, which sends a pending reward before creating a new one ("About to create freeplay sparks reward message but there was a pending one, so sending that one now").

The null-pick path is the second half of GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal 0x005AE29C. Before asking the activity it decides, in order: a debug-forced activity (+0x91) that is not the current one; the requested activity (+0x90) that is not the current one; a spark change or no current activity at all; then, only when no behaviour is running (0x005AE352) and no sparks reward is pending (0x005AE362), the strategy's WantsToEnd. Then it asks IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior 0x005B387C and decides again on the answer: a null pick logs "ActivityFreeplay.ChooseNextBehavior.NoBehaviorChosenWhileRunning: Picking new activity because '%s' chose behavior '%s'. This activity is not allowed to be repicked." and jumps back to the pick with PickNewActivityForSpark's third argument false (0x005AE75C); a pick that is not the behaviour already running - IBehavior+0xa1, the flag Init sets (0x005BCD06) and Stop clears (0x005BD10C) - logs "NewBehaviorChosenWhileRunning" and jumps back with it true (0x005AE702), unless a sparks reward is pending. That third argument is read at 0x005ADCA2: the activity that is still current is only eligible again when it is passed true and its strategy does not want to end.

So an activity whose chooser yields nothing is dropped at once and barred from the re-pick, and an activity that wants to end survives only while the same behaviour keeps running - the moment its chooser would start a different one, the activity goes instead. This stack kept the activity and only stopped the unrunnable behaviour; the tick's middle is now the engine's loop.

records.title: The feature gate, and where boredomMultiplier is actually read
records.provenance: WantsToStart, CozmoFeatureGate and BehaviorPounceOnMotion, read, against the shipped configs
records.authority: IActivityStrategy::WantsToStart 0x005B529C, CozmoFeatureGate::IsFeatureEnabled 0x006A679C and BehaviorPounceOnMotion's constructor 0x005F7F91, read
evidence: The feature gate is the first thing WantsToStart tests: the flag at strategy+0x38 and then CozmoFeatureGate::IsFeatureEnabled(featureType), refusing outright when it says no (0x005B52A8..0x005B52BC). IsFeatureEnabled 0x006A679C turns the enum into its name, lowercases it and looks it up; the list comes from config/features.json, the path at 0x00BE8449. The shipped file has seventeen entries, with Invalid, SparksGatherCubes and Bouncer off and the rest on, and the only two activities that name a gate - singing.json and sparksCozmoSings.json - name Singing, which is on. This stack now parses featureGate and consults FeatureGates.

boredomMultiplier is not a scoring field at all. The string appears once in the whole binary, inside BehaviorPounceOnMotion's constructor (0x005F8384, among that class's own keys maxNoGroundMotionBeforeBored_* and maxTimeBehaviorTimeout_Sec), so the only reader is that behaviour, reading its own config. The one place the shipped data sets it is hiking.json's scoring block for Hiking_PounceOnMotion, which is an activity's scoring entry and never reaches the behaviour's config - neither pounceOnMotion config carries the key. So the value is dead data, and recording it without applying it is correct.

The pyramid strategy's 300 s cooldown (0x43960000) is already recorded; there is no separate random factor in it beyond the RandDbl(randomness) every strategy gets when its cooldown passes, which this stack applies in RandomizeCooldown.

records.title: The needsActionID hook and desired-from-objects ordering
records.provenance: CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects, IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted, the two ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig routines and every call site, read
records.authority: ActivityFreeplay::CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects 0x005ADF4C, IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted 0x005BE40C, IBehavior::IBehavior 0x005BBCAA, IBehavior::ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005BBAE8, IActivity::ReadConfig 0x005B2A9C, IActivity::ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005B3094, the sixteen NeedActionCompleted call sites and ActivityGatherCubes::Update 0x005AF2F0, read
evidence: The desired activity from what is around is a plain four-way switch. CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects 0x005ADF4C takes the two booleans and reads the name at +0x68 for face and cube, +0x69 for a face alone, +0x6A for a cube alone and +0x6B for neither, storing the pick at +0x90. That is the order DesiredActivityNames carries here - faceAndCube, faceOnly, cubeOnly, noFaceNoCube - and DesiredActivityFromObjects already matched it.

The needs-action hook belongs to the behaviour, not the activity. IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted 0x005BE40C is four instructions: when the caller passes Invalid the behaviour's own id at +0x68 is used (the cbnz at 0x005BE40C), and the result goes to NeedsManager::RegisterNeedsActionCompleted through the robot. IBehavior's constructor fills +0x68 at 0x005BBCAA from ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005BBAE8, which reads the config's needsActionID string and converts it; twenty-two shipped behaviour configs carry the key.

Sixteen behaviours call it. Ten pass Invalid and so report their own configured action - KnockOverCubes at TransitionToPlayingReaction but only when the stack came apart (the flag at +0x14c gates the objective and the report together, 0x005C3950), PopAWheelie on the docking success beside objective PoppedWheelie (0x005C7E14), RollBlock::TransitionToRollSuccess, StackBlocks::TransitionToPlayingFinalAnim, CubeLiftWorkout::EndIteration, BuildPyramid::TransitionToReactingToPyramid, FistBump::UpdateInternal, PeekABoo::TransitionExit, TrackLaser::StopInternal and the singing behaviour's last step, which falls back to CozmoSings when its config has none (0x005EF7CA). Six name one outright: PickupCube 0x1F from BehaviorExploreBringCubeToBeacon::TransitionToObjectPickedUp, StackCube 0x2A from the explorer's stacking callback (0x005E14B6), GuardDogLose/Win/NoInteraction 0x15/0x16/0x17 from BehaviorGuardDog::RecordResult, PlacedOnSide 0x2F and BoredOnSide 0x30 from BehaviorReactToRobotOnSide, and DizzyMedium/DizzySoft 0x0F/0x10 from BehaviorReactToRobotShaken. One activity reports directly to the manager: ActivityGatherCubes::Update passes GatherCubes 0x14 when every cube is in a beacon (0x005AF2F0). The enum names come from the EnumToString table at 0x01033D40, 0x57 entries.

An activity's own needsActionID is dead data. IActivity::ReadConfig stores it at IActivity+0x1C (0x005B2A9C) and nothing loads that word again: no IActivity or Activity* method reads +0x1C on the activity, and the one activity that reports an action names it itself. So the three shipped activity-level ids - PyramidCompleted, PyramidCompleted_Sparked, CozmoSingsCompleted_Sparked - are never reported, and neither is the pyramid behaviour's, since no pyramid behaviour config carries the key. This stack reported the activity's id when the activity ended; that call is gone, and the behaviours report their own through BehaviorNeedsActions.
